Date: 2026-07-19
Start: 08:32 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Solanis Head of Security), Leah Ortiz (Solanis CTO), Samir Patel (Solanis Platform Eng)
summary: Discovery focused on Solanis' security and compliance requirements for evaluating Redwood across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment models. Key topics: SOC2 / ISO evidence, SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logging retention and access, encryption and KMS integration, data residency and retention policies. Solanis is leaning toward Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads but wants proof points and a pilot plan.
topics: SSO / SAML integration and SCIM provisioning
Data residency and retention policy options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and pricing
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. quick check — audio good?
[00:07] Marcus: Yeah loud and clear, Marcus here. thanks.
[00:10] Priya: Hi all, thanks. we wanted to run through your security posture and questions, and we can call out differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
[00:18] Leah: Great, high level first - we are evaluating vendor for our inference layer for PII-sensitive analytics. main asks are SOC 2 and ISO, SSO, KMS, retention and audit logs.
[00:30] Jordan: Perfect, that aligns with a lot of customers. quick q on scope - is this for internal dev workloads or customer-facing production?
[00:36] Leah: Primarily production for customer-facing features, some internal models too. regulatory concerns, so we'll need data residency for EU and US.
[00:44] Samir: And we have HIPAA-ish constraints, we need encryption at rest, BYOK where possible and auditability.
[00:50] Jordan: Got it. on compliance, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we maintain ISO 27001 — we can share the certs and the controls matrix. I'll email those after the call.
[01:00] Marcus: When you say "share" is that the full report or a summary? legal tends to want the full attestation or a redacted version.
[01:06] Jordan: Usually we provide the SOC 2 report with an NDA and a summary controls matrix publicly; we can do the redacted report via our security process. I'll note that action item.
[01:14] Priya: On the deployment side, Hosted is fastest but for regulated workloads customers pick Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our infra with tenancy isolation and optional VPC peering, Private is full customer-managed control plane and on-prem if needed.
[01:29] Leah: Do Dedicated nodes live in our VPC or in Redwood's?
[01:33] Priya: For Dedicated we host the compute in Redwood-managed projects but you get network isolation and we support VPC peering and private endpoints, so traffic can traverse your VPC. For full control we do Private which installs a control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:46] Samir: Okay that helps. how do you handle SSO? we use SAML with Okta and SCIM for provisioning.
[01:53] Priya: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. we have sample metadata and a step-by-step integration guide. role mapping and RBAC are configurable — you can map SAML assertions to Redwood roles, and we've seen customers implement least-privilege using teams + route-level permissions.
[02:08] Marcus: Any gotchas around SCIM for large orgs? we have 5k users and complex groups.
[02:12] Priya: SCIM handles groups but we recommend starting with a service account and sync scope limited to groups used for Redwood. large orgs often do staged provisioning. we'll share our SCIM docs.
[02:20] Leah: Audit logs — we need immutable logs, retention at least 1 year and export to our SIEM.
[02:26] Jordan: Redwood provides audit logs for admin actions and API usage. for Dedicated and Private you can configure log exports to your S3 or SIEM (via syslog/forwarder). retention is configurable; hosted default is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an addon.
[02:38] Samir: Can we get write-once logs or HSM-backed immutability?
[02:42] Priya: For immutability you can export to your storage with write-once policies; we also support integration with partner SIEMs. HSM-backed immutability isn't in the standard hosted product but for Private we can support customer-controlled logging and HSM integrations.
[02:56] Marcus: Encryption - at rest and in transit, and BYOK?
[03:00] Jordan: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. at rest we encrypt with provider keys by default; BYOK is supported via KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM approaches for on-prem.
[03:13] Leah: If we use BYOK, do you ever see keys leave our control?
[03:16] Priya: Keys stay in your KMS, we fetch ephemeral wrapping keys, but you retain control and can revoke. for Private deployments keys can be entirely customer-managed.
[03:25] Samir: What about model caching and KV cache — any risk of leakage across tenants?
[03:29] Priya: We partition KV caches per deployment/tenant. Dedicated has strict tenancy isolation and per-customer cache namespaces, Private is entirely customer-owned. but we do recommend redaction in prompts for sensitive PII, and we have prefix caching controls.
[03:45] Marcus: Logging and access — how granular is RBAC? can we restrict by route/model and by token-level?
[03:52] Jordan: Yes, RBAC supports org/teams/roles and you can set route-level permissions. token-level billing data is visible in the console for owners only — audit logs link actions to tokens and users.
[04:05] Leah: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain datasets. do you have region isolation?
[04:10] Priya: We have region-specific deployments. Hosted can pin requests to EU regions, Dedicated gives you capacity in the region, Private deploys in your own region or on-prem. We'll document region options and provide deployment timeframes.
[04:22] Samir: About data retention policies — can you auto-delete request logs after a TTL?
[04:26] Jordan: Yes, log retention TTLs are configurable per account; for hosted defaults we have 90-day, but for enterprise you can set shorter or longer, and for Dedicated/Private you control retention fully.
[04:36] Marcus: Incident response and breach notifications?
[04:39] Jordan: We have an IR policy, SLA notification processes, and we commit to notifying customers within defined windows per contract. we'll share the IR playbook redacted.
[04:49] Leah: Do you have pen test results or do you run third-party assessments?
[04:52] Priya: We run annual third-party pen tests and can share summaries; for Dedicated/Private we can coordinate scoping with your security team for additional tests.
[05:02] Marcus: Ok a couple of procurement things — contract language around data ownership and indemnity, plus security addendums.
[05:09] Jordan: Standard enterprise MSA includes data ownership clauses and security addendum; we can surface standard SAs and negotiate.
[05:15] Samir: If we prototype on Hosted first and move to Dedicated, is migration smooth?
[05:19] Priya: Yes we support model variant compatibility and migration tooling, but we recommend a staged approach: pilot on Hosted, then Dedicated for steady production, then Private only if you need full control. SD testing helps.
[05:30] Leah: Latency/cost tradeoffs — can you provide expected L40ms vs throughputs?
[05:34] Priya: We'll need sample prompts and sequence lengths. we asked for traffic profile, that will let us pick quantization, batch size and GPUs. we'll run a baseline benchmark for you.
[05:46] Marcus: Are there any known limitations with Okta SAML + SCIM? we've had issues with group attribute mapping in other vendors.
[05:52] Priya: We have a mapping guide. group mapping sometimes needs tweaks but it's standard. we can share sample mappings that other large customers used.
[06:00] Jordan: Quick recap and next steps?
[06:03] Leah: Yes please.
[06:05] Jordan: I'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts and the security whitepaper, Priya will send SAML/SCIM guides and sample metadata. Priya will also scope the benchmark and we want Samir to share traffic profile. we'll aim to have a pricing/ Dedicated sizing follow-up week of 7/27.
[06:20] Marcus: sounds good.
[06:22] Samir: I'll pull a sample packet and retention requirements and send by Friday.
[06:26] Leah: ok thanks all.
[06:28] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs.
[42:00] [call end]
